headline: Create one new node per original before following edges
statement: Given a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy of the graph. Every copied node must be a new object with the same value and copied neighbor connections; no returned object may reuse an original node. Return None for an empty graph. Trainer input is a 1-indexed adjacency list; the entry node has value 1.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
constraints: Node values are unique integers 1 through n.
The graph is connected, with no self-loops or repeated edges.
intuition: Make one new node for each original node, and remember that mapping. Before exploring a neighbor, create its copy if needed. Connect copies to copies according to the original edges. Recording a copy before exploring its neighbors prevents cycles from creating duplicate copies forever.
approach: Create the entry clone and queue its original.
For every original edge, create and enqueue an unseen neighbor clone.
Append the mapped neighbor clone to the current clone’s neighbors.
correctness: Each discovered original has one distinct clone before any edge can revisit it. Processing an original appends exactly one cloned connection per original neighbor, preserving the adjacency structure and occurrence count. Connectedness ensures all nodes are discovered; only new clone objects are linked, establishing a deep copy.
bruteForce: Recursively clone every neighbor with no memoization. Cycles cause infinite recursion, and repeated paths incorrectly create multiple copies of one node.

complexity.space: O(V+E) including the cloned graph; O(V) auxiliary
complexity.explanation: Every node is queued once and every adjacency entry is copied once. The map and queue are linear in vertex count.

pitfalls: Record a clone before exploring its neighbors.
Return the clone of the entry, not the original.
One original must map to one clone even when multiple paths reach it.
